notes.decision: Translated 'The Sun' as running header. May refer back to the previous chapter's topic (the sun) which served as a section-marker label, or be the running title for this group of kephalaia. Same root as ⲡⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ ('the Radiance') in glossary — preserves verbal-emission semantics ('the shining one').

Translated 'recompense' (= Sah. ⲃⲉⲕⲉ 'wages, reward, recompense'). The lexeme structures the entire kephalaion: vengeful 'recompense' for sin (lines 2-19) is contrasted with disciplinary 'reproof' (ⲭⲡⲓⲟ, line 26). The text argues that what the worldly call 'recompense' against sinners is properly named 'reproof of strictness' bringing them to repentance. Distinguished from homophone ⲃⲁⲕⲉ in 'wage' sense — here the punitive-retributive register dominates.
Translated 'wrath' (cf. accumulated ⲧⲃⲗ̄ⲕⲉ 'wrath' from Sah. ⲃⲱⲗⲕ̄ 'be angry'). Recurs five times on this page (lines 4, 8, 10, 14, 19) as the affective core of false 'recompense.'
Greek loanword φλύαρος 'foolish talker, babbler' verbalized with ⲣ̄- prefix. Translated 'play the fool' to capture the Greek register of empty/foolish speech (cf. 1 Tim 5:13 φλύαροι).

Translated 'the chastisement of wrath.' ⲧⲍⲉⲡⲧ likely from a root meaning 'rebuke/chastisement' or related to ⲥⲏⲡⲧ̄ 'preparation, fitting thing.' The contextual pairing with ⲃⲱⲗⲕ ('wrath') and the parallel disciplinary register of ⲭⲡⲓⲟ later in the page support 'chastisement' as functional translation.

Greek loanword γνώμη 'judgment, opinion, resolve.' Standard philosophical/legal term for considered judgment. The disciple acting 'unto the γνώμη of his brothers' = submitting to fraternal communal discernment.

Translated tentatively as 'a harshness.' Possibly Lyc. for ⲟⲩⲟⲉⲓⲍⲉ or a form related to ⲟⲩⲟⲓⲉ 'sharp, harsh.' Pairing with ⲛ̄ϣⲁⲧ 'severity' confirms negative-affective register. Confidence low; flagged for parallels.

The pivotal definitional formula: 'its name is the reproof of the strictness which brings unto repentance.' This reframes what worldly retribution misnames 'recompense' (ⲃⲁⲕⲉ) as properly being 'reproof' (ⲭⲡⲓⲟ) — the disciplinary corrective of fraternal severity oriented toward μετάνοια. Standard Manichaean ecclesiastical disciplinary theology.

Translated 'applying' tentatively. The form is ambiguous: could be (a) Lyc. variant of ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'select, choose' (the physician selecting medicines); (b) a verb of medical application; (c) qualitative 'be skilled/expert.' Medical context with ⲧⲟⲟⲧϩ̄ 'his hand' and ⲍⲛ̄ ⲧ[medicines] supports an applying/wielding sense. Etymology uncertain; flagged.
Lyc. habitual 3sg.m ϣⲁϩ- + ⲧⲗϭⲁⲩ (= ⲧⲁⲗϭⲟ + 3pl) 'he treats them, he applies medicine to them.' Standard medical-causative; the wise physician 'habitually treats' the wounds.

Translated 'hot' / 'bitter.' The pair ⲍⲏⲙ (= ϩⲏⲙ 'hot') and ⲕⲏⲃ ('bitter,' in glossary) forms the medicinal antithesis: wounds requiring different temperatures and tastes of remedy. Direct gustatory-correspondence: certain spiritual conditions require 'hot' correction (intense reproof), others 'bitter' (humbling). Standard ancient medical schema (humoral hot/cold + sweet/bitter).
